text:
observability-bot: [ALERT] prod/cluster-eu-west: latency P95 ↑ 3.2x, error rate +1.1%. KV prefix cache global hit-rate collapsed 68% -> 5% in ~6m.
oncall: on it — paging infra leads.
Maya L: confirming from traces — a lot more full-KV reads, tail latency for kv.Read has spikes ~200ms. Routing shows many requests routed to shard-12.
Samir: grabbed a quick profile from one node (top lines). Looks like kernel selector fell back to generic matmul path for a lot of requests. Also batching count jumped.
Samir: ```
# perf summary (sampled)
service/main.go: kv.Read 42%
runtime/alloc 12%
kernel_selector.cpp::select_kernel 8% (fallback_generic)
batcher.cpp::process_batch 6% (batch_size median 48)
```
Dmitri: I pulled the config diff from last deploy — there was a heuristic tweak rolled yesterday 03:12 UTC to reduce latency under high conc by increasing target batch_size to 48. Also a knobs change lowered kv.cache.max_prefix_items from 2e6 -> 5e5 (prob to free mem).
Dmitri: diff snippet: ```
- batcher.target_batch_size: 8
+ batcher.target_batch_size: 48
- kv.cache.max_prefix_items: 2000000
+ kv.cache.max_prefix_items: 500000
```
Eve: that explains the hit-rate collapse — fewer cached prefixes + larger batches causing more divergent prefixes entering batches, so cache priming/eviction churn. Also saw an uptick in cold-tenant traffic (noisy neighbor) on shard-12.
Maya L: I reran a micro-repro on canary with the new batcher setting and instrumented kernel selection counts — when batch_size > 32, selector picks fallback kernel ~72% of the time for our Llama-like models. On smaller batches it's the optimized kernel. So the batching heuristic change regressed kernel selection and amplified KV misses.
Samir: quick numbers from canary run: ```
metrics:
  prefix_hit_rate: 94% (batch 8) -> 12% (batch 48)
  kernel_fast_path_pct: 88% (batch 8) -> 27% (batch 48)
  p95 latency: 18ms -> 120ms
```
oncall: mitigation plan?
Dmitri: immediate rollback candidate: revert batcher.target_batch_size to 8 and restore kv.cache.max_prefix_items to 2e6. That should stop thrash and make selector choose fast kernels again.
Eve: also can enable an emergency routing rule to avoid shard-12 for noisy tenants for 30m (soft drain) while we stabilize.
Maya L: I'll prepare a config revert and a canary deploy to two nodes. Need approval for rolling-restart of leader routers.
oncall: approved. Do the revert. Notify if anything changes.
Samir: pushed revert PR and started canary. Logs show prefix_hit_rate climbing back to ~70% on canary after revert. Kernel selector fast-path restored.
Maya L: canary looks healthy after 8m — p95 back to normal. Rolling revert starting.
Eve: postmortem items: (1) add unit/regression test for kernel selector vs batch_size distribution; (2) prevent large batch target changes without kv cache hysteresis; (3) add autoscaling-friendly prefetch/priming for noisy tenants.
Dmitri: also add alerting: delta in prefix_hit_rate > 20% over 5m should page runtime oncall.
Samir: noted. I'll capture profiling artifacts and attach to the PR.
oncall: Thanks team — rolling revert is complete, cluster metrics stabilized. Will follow up with a short incident write-up. :thumbsup:
